newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends slightly down on Deng.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends slightly down on Deng.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed down slightly on Thursday after falling sharply at the opening on the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, brokers said.
They said overseas selling pushed the index down early, but it had rebounded by noon on domestic bargain-hunting.
The B index fell 0.455 points or 0.7 percent to 64.675 points on volume of 40.7 million shares worth $17.1 million.

The domestic A share index rose slightly, up 2.781 points or 0.28 percent to 1007.731 points after opening close to the 10 percent limit-down level. Volume was 884.6 million shares worth eight billion yuan.
Brokers said Deng's death would not greatly influence the stock market in the next few sessions.
"The performance of the market depends on how much money there is here and on listed firms' results. Sudden events just have temporary impact on the market," one broker said.
"The index is likely to consolidate in the short term and the speculative mood will cool to some extent," a second broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded, with 23 up, six flat and 13 down.
Shanghai Goods & Materials Trade Centre Co Ltd was the biggest loser on expectations of poor 1996 results, slipping $0.016 or 8.69 percent to $0.168 on volume of 232,000 shares.

Tientsin Marine Shipping Co Ltd was the most active share on overseas institutional liquidation on concerns about its lawsuit announced on Monday. It fell $0.026 or 6.1 percent to $0.40 on volume of 5.6 million shares.
Shanghai's A shares reversed early losses in active trading on improved sentiment with fresh capital flowing into the market, brokers said.
But the SSE 30 blue-chip index fell 5.286 points or 0.2 percent to 2642.133 points.
Shanghai Electrical Apparatus Co Ltd was the star on rumours it had financial restructuring plans, soaring 0.52 yuan or 10 percent limit-up to 5.67 yuan on volume of 8.8 million shares.
